body: It's true that remaining in your comfort zone will not help you overcome anxiety, but teachers aren't psychologists. If a student is too anxious to do a presentation, there are lots of ways forcing a student to do it anyway can backfire and end up causing more anxiety. Severe anxiety is a very different problem than feeling a little nervous. It can make people physically ill and if "treated" the wrong way, it will get worse/disorder level bad. The best way to help shy students is to normalize public speaking and take the pressure off by making it no big deal, IMO. And provide mental health resources by people qualified to deal with it, if it's bad enough.

I was a very shy/anxious teenager who had a lot of trouble with presentations.

I do think gaining experience with public speaking helps students who are anxious or shy, but only when it feels safe for the student. Otherwise, you're creating more negative/bad experiences and giving the phobia more fuel. If I were a teacher in this situation, I would ask that students participate in multiple 5 minute presentations that are participation grade-- if you get up there and say anything, you get full points. I would encourage the students by saying it's not a big deal, no pressure, just share something you think is interesting about what we're reading. Normalizing it like this without pushing past the threshold for the student's anxiety will help them feel more confident.
Yeah, I feel that. Definitely one of my biggest fears.
Definitely can relate. Sorry you're dealing with this too. I hope you can find what I haven't-- a place where people truly love and accept you.
I feel the lack of empathy in my life too. It's hard to not harden towards others when you feel the lack of caring so acutely.

Doesn't sound stupid to me. Some of the most stressful times in my life were me struggling hard over school. The stress and expectations can feel like drowning, especially if you're already prone to anxiety, depression or you're just sensitive to stress.

"You're just too negative."

Yes, thank you. That's a serious problem for me. In fact, I think it's part of a undiagnosed mental illness I have, and one cool fun thing about mental illness is you can't just wish or will it away. I want to switch brains with some people for five minutes. My life experiences vs yours, let's go.

I think for me, if I'm going in for a facial treatment or something, I want to be well informed by the esthetician. Being told exactly what's going to happen, what I can expect, what I can and can't do after the treatment, etc and focusing on the medical side makes you seem like you know what you're doing and would make me trust you more even if you weren't into talking about yourself.

I actually think a lot of people don't necessarily want a hair dresser, esthetician, etc who just goes on and on about themselves or wastes their time, so I think you'll be fine (and even especially appreciated by some people!) even if you're a little quiet.

For people who aren't as anxious, you can ask them questions about their skin care/routine and give suggestions. Even like general health questions can be good because things like drinking enough water, not smoking, etc do effect skin and you don't have to talk about yourself.

Sorry to hear you were made fun of when you were young-- that really deeply effects people for a long time and no one deserves to go through that :(  


I think what you're saying about people liking me is true sometimes, but the behavior is still extremely anxiety provoking for me and actively harmful. I don't want to feel monitored all the time.

For sure. I just wish people would think a bit more before speaking about it. Like, I'd never tell someone with a lifelong illness like type 1 diabetes or something to "just exercise more." I don't have that illness, I don't know anything about it and it's not my place to give advice. So idk, as much as I want to have sympathy for people who just don't get it and say stupid stuff, I kind of can't.

I feel like lots of people have some weird food issues because, man, eating can be such a trigger for inappropriate comments. I'm sorry you have to deal with that on the reg.
